subject: Request: timestamped subprocessor manifest + onshore fallback plan
messages:
From: Laura Grant <laura.grant@fintrust.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: timestamped subprocessor manifest + onshore fallback plan

Karthik,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. As part of FinTrust's vendor review ahead of our compliance committee on Friday, we need a couple of things from Redwood to close the intake: 

- A timestamped subprocessor manifest (xlsx) that lists all third parties that process or route EU-origin data, the data paths they touch, and any encryption/split-key controls in place.
- KMS / HSM attestation or the most recent evidence we can rely on for key custody and export controls (PDF).
- A short note (1 paragraph) describing onshore fallback options if an EU-region subprocessor becomes unavailable.

Can you confirm you can provide the manifest and attestation by EOD Thursday (2027-04-29 PT)? If you have an internal doc with the fallback runbook we can reference, that would be very helpful.

Also please indicate if there are any subprocessors that perform transient telemetry logging outside the EU — we need to flag those to our data protection officer.

Laura Grant
Head of Vendor Risk, FinTrust
laura.grant@fintrust.com

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Laura Grant <laura.grant@fintrust.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: timestamped subprocessor manifest + onshore fallback plan

Laura —

Appreciate the clear list. We can absolutely get that to you. Quick plan: 

1) I'm attaching a draft 'subprocessor manifest' (redwood_subprocessor_manifest_20270426.xlsx) that includes processing purpose, country of processing, whether the vendor touches KV cache / telemetry, and the last attestation date.

2) KMS attestation (KMS_attestation_Q1_2027.pdf) is attached — it's our Q1 evidence package including HSM provider contact and key rotation cadence.

3) Onshore fallback: we have a short-runbook (excerpt below) that describes automatic routing to a zonal onshore pair + degraded-throughput SLA. We'll include the full runbook in the package if helpful.

Excerpt — Onshore fallback (summary):
- If an EU subprocessor or transit link fails, traffic is routed to our EU-dedicated onshore pool by policy. For customers requiring strict residency we provide an on-prem or VPC option as an assured fallback. Temporary routing to a US region is only used when explicitly consented for exceptional continuity; in those cases we apply additional encryption-in-transit controls and inform customers and DPOs.

A couple of quick clarifying asks so we give you the exact matrix you need:
- Do you want us to include service accounts and ephemeral cloud functions in the manifest (they're listed in a separate sheet right now)?
- Can we upload the package to your secure S3 link or should we attach here?

I expect Kimberly to add any legal redline notes; Marissa will verify the telemetry columns.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Product Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Laura Grant <laura.grant@fintrust.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: timestamped subprocessor manifest + onshore fallback plan

Laura / team —

Thanks, Karthik. I'm looping in a couple of quick legal notes so FinTrust's counsel can baseline expectations before the committee: 

- We'll include service account/service-principal rows but mark them as internal ephemeral processors; they'll be clearly flagged in the manifest as not-subcontractors per se.
- Export-control note: Redwood performs key wrapping for cross-border transit; the attestation gives our current HSM provider and the wrap/unwrap locations. If FinTrust needs an additional localization addendum (e.g., contractual onshore-only key custody), we can propose language but that will require an amendment to the DPA.
- We will mark telemetry flows that contain low-sensitivity metrics vs. those that may contain hashed tokens/identifiers. If you need token-level pseudonymization, that is doable but will require engineering lead time — we can outline that next week.

Attaching the two files Karthik put together; I've also added a one-page legal summary inside the manifest tab called 'Legal-Summary'.

If FinTrust prefers a secure upload, we can place the package on a pre-auth S3 link and send you a HubSpot ticket link for tracking.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Grant <laura.grant@fintrust.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: timestamped subprocessor manifest + onshore fallback plan

Hi Kim / Karthik —

Received the attachments and the summary — thank you. The committee asked for the pre-auth S3 upload rather than email attachments for their record-keeping. If you can send the link and a HubSpot tracking ID, we'll put it on the agenda for Friday.

Two small follow-ups: 
1) Please flag any processors that have transient telemetry outside EU in the manifest (even if hashed).
2) If you can add an explicit 'time-to-failover' metric to the runbook excerpt (expected minutes to route and expected impact on throughput), that will help us evaluate continuity posture.

If you can get the upload and the small edits to us by EOD Thursday our compliance lead can close the review.

Best,
Laura
Head of Vendor Risk, FinTrust
